1.name: Pressure tube
1.note: The body of the damper. Its bore guides the piston and holds the oil and the gas charge.

2.name: Base cap
2.note: Closes the gas end of the tube and carries the lower eye ring.

3.name: Eye ring
3.note: The mounting loop at each end. One fixes the damper to the wheel, the other to the body.

4.name: Eye bush
4.note: A rubber bush in each eye. It lets the damper tilt a little and softens the highest-frequency shocks.

5.name: Inner sleeve
5.note: The steel sleeve inside each bush that the mounting bolt passes through.

6.name: Gas fill plug
6.note: A rubber plug in the base cap. It seals the nitrogen in after the factory charge.

7.name: Floating piston
7.note: Separates the oil from the nitrogen. It slides to take up the rod's volume and keeps the oil under pressure, so it cannot cavitate.

8.name: O-ring
8.note: Seals the floating piston to the tube so oil and gas never mix.

9.name: Piston
9.note: The working piston, with three ports for each direction. Oil is forced through these ports, and that flow resistance is the damping.

10.name: Piston band
10.note: A low-friction ring that guides the piston in the tube and stops oil leaking past its rim.

11.name: Compression shim
11.note: A stack of thin discs over the compression ports. They bend open under oil pressure, which makes the force flatten out past the knee at high speed.

12.name: Rebound shim
12.note: The same idea on the rebound ports. A stiffer stack gives the damper more force when it extends.

13.name: Clamp washer
13.note: Pins the centre of each shim stack, so only its outer edge can flex.

14.name: Hex nut
14.note: Holds the piston and shim stack on the end of the rod.

15.name: Piston rod
15.note: Carries the wheel's motion to the piston. The volume it displaces is what the floating piston has to absorb.

16.name: Rebound stop ring
16.note: A shoulder on the rod that meets the buffer at full extension.

17.name: Rebound buffer
17.note: A polyurethane cushion that softens the end of the extension stroke.

18.name: Rod guide
18.note: Closes the top of the tube and holds the rod bushing and seals in line with the bore.

19.name: Guide bushing
19.note: A low-friction bearing that keeps the rod straight against the sideways loads of the suspension.

20.name: Rod seal
20.note: The main seal on the rod. It keeps the high-pressure oil inside.

21.name: Dust wiper
21.note: Wipes dirt and water off the rod as it retracts, protecting the rod seal.

22.name: O-ring
22.note: Seals the rod guide to the tube bore.

23.name: Retaining ring
23.note: A circlip in a groove in the tube that holds the rod guide against the oil pressure.

24.name: Bump stop
24.note: A foam cushion on the rod that takes over when the suspension bottoms out, adding stiffness near full compression.

25.name: Dust shield
25.note: A sheet-steel sleeve over the tube that protects the rod and seals from stones and dirt.
